Subject: Novatia pilot readiness — benchmark reads, verified profiles & ops checklist

Alexandra — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we all have the same playbook.

Key takeaways from the discovery:
- Primary flow: search + snippet generation for knowledge-base articles (avg doc length ~600 tokens).
- Target SLA: 300ms p95 per user-facing generation; batch background re-ranking can tolerate higher latency.
- Expected QPS during pilot: 25–40 RPS with burst to 80 for peak indexing windows.

Redwood-recommended slate (shortlist for pilot):
- rwd-llama-13b-q4f16 — best cost/quality balance for snippet generation at 512 tokens; good NLU.
- rwd-mistral-7b-v2-qat — lower cost, acceptable for re-ranking and short completions.
- rwd-guanaco-30b-8bit — fallback for high-quality longer responses (reserve capacity).

Verified performance profiles (Redwood-verified):
- Profiles include TPS, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), and memory footprint for the sequence lengths we discussed.
- See attached PDF (redwood_verified_profiles.pdf) and the console link below for per-model traces.

Benchmark links (evidence we ran with your prompt slices):
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1nVx-ExampleBenchLinks (pilot pack + raw traces)
- Trace bundle attached: novatia_benchmark_traces.zip (contains perf traces, token counts, and run configs).

Quality/regression notes to be aware of:
- We observed a small regression vs. baseline for named-entity consistency on the 13B at very long contexts (>1,200 tokens); we recommend running the 13B with prefix KV caching enabled and adding the prompt guardrail in prompt_set_v1.json.
- Hallucination rate on the 7b variant was low for extractive tasks but higher for open-ended summarization — we flagged specific prompts in the prompt set.

Operational checklist for pilot (next steps):
1) Novatia accepts the pilot model slate and desired SLOs (reply with lanes: user-generation / re-rank / bulk-index).
2) We’ll provision a 2-week dedicated pool (Dev credits) and share a preconfigured runbook.
3) Camila to provide an ops runbook addendum for autoscaling thresholds and batching knobs.
4) You share any compliance artifacts we need to mirror (retention, redaction rules).

Attachments: novatia_benchmark_traces.zip, novatia_prompt_set_v1.json, redwood_verified_profiles.pdf

If that matches, can we lock model slate + SLOs by Friday (May 28)? I’ll book a 30-min kickoff with infra + eng.

Best,
Rafael

Alexandra — quick technical answers to Rafael’s slate and your questions.

Memory footprint & cost (summary):
- rwd-mistral-7b-v2-qat: ~14GB GPU memory (float16 exec), best for low-cost re-rank and short snippets. Strong candidate if you want minimal reserved capacity.
- rwd-llama-13b-q4f16: ~28–32GB depending on kernel packing; provides the best balance for 512-token completions with processed throughput ~20–30 TPS per GPU in our dedicated configs.
- rwd-guanaco-30b-8bit: ~48GB (8-bit) — higher latency but higher answer fidelity for long-form. Use as fallback.

Latency evidence (Redwood-verified traces):
- rwd-llama-13b-q4f16 @ 512 tokens: p50=85ms, p95=310ms, p99=480ms (measured on A100-80GB equip with continuous batching at 25 RPS).
- rwd-mistral-7b-v2-qat @ 256 tokens: p50=45ms, p95=120ms, p99=210ms.

Notes & recommended ops knobs:
- Batching: enable adaptive batching with a max batch size of 32 and sub-ms batching timeout of 5ms for user-facing lane to hit p95 targets while retaining cost efficiency.
- KV prefix caching: enable for conversations/long-context flows to drop effective per-token time for repeated prefixes by ~30%.
- Fallback policy: route to mistral-7b for non-critical re-rank jobs when dedicated 13B pool is saturated.

Prompt set considerations and regression guardrails:
- We flagged three prompts in the prompt set where entity leakage occurred; the attached prompt_set_v1.json includes a deterministic template to mitigate.
- Add nightly regression evals (we can provide Redwood’s eval harness) that run a 500-sample quality test against your production prompts — alert on >4% drift in entity F1 or >7% increase in hallucination rate.

Ops artifacts I’ll attach to the kickoff folder: autoscale.json, batch-config.yaml, and a short runbook for incident triage.

— Camila
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai

- Capacity: provision 2x A100-80GB equivalents for initial 2-week pilot (target 30 RPS avg; autoscale to 75 RPS burst).
- SLO: p95 <= 350ms for user-generation lane (we’ll tune batching/timeouts to hit this). p99 targets tracked but not guaranteed for pilot.
- Security: we support per-tenant KMS — legal to confirm contract clause; please share redaction/retention doc.

Concrete next steps:
1) Novatia confirms model slate + SLOs (reply to this thread).
2) Novatia sends retention & KMS requirements (Doc or slide).

4) Book 30-min kickoff with Novatia infra + our infra/solutions (I booked 2027-05-27 10:00 AM PT as a tentative slot — please confirm or propose another).
